identity.name: Vandal Kingdom
alt_names: Kingdom of the Vandals and Alans

land.text: coastal Numidia and parts of Mauretania, the land the Vandals kept under the treaty of 435

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's first Vandal shape starts in 439; the Vandal Kingdom page dates the treaty and the capital Hippo Regius to 435. Carthage and the rest of Proconsular Africa follow in 439, Byzacena and Tripolitania in 442.

land.text: Africa Proconsularis, Numidia, Tripolitania and the islands: the Praetorian prefecture of Africa created in April 534 (Vandalic War page); inland Numidia and Mauretania stayed with the Mauri

successors.note: Sardinia, Corsica and the Balearics were taken after Tricamarum; Lilybaeum in Sicily had gone to the Ostrogoths.

capitals.name: Hippo Regius (Annaba)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Hippo Regius (435-439)'; the city fell after a siege of '14 months' begun in 430.

capitals.name: Carthage
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Carthage (439-534)'; captured by surprise on 19 October 439.

rulers.name: Gaiseric
rulers.note: King from 428 on the page's list (428-477); the infobox gives 435-477. Died at Carthage on 25 January 477, aged 88.

rulers.name: Hilderic
rulers.note: Executed in 533 when the Byzantine army approached Carthage.

rulers.name: Gelimer
rulers.note: Surrendered at Mount Pappua in March 534.

correction.text: the Mauretanian and Numidian coast of the 435 treaty, without the Balearic Islands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 435-438. The Vandal Kingdom page: the treaty of 435 gave 'coastal Numidia and parts of Mauretania', with Hippo Regius the capital 435-439. Cliopatria's 439 shape (85,012 km2: the Mauretanian and Numidian coast plus the Balearics) is read as that grant. The Balearics are not on the page until 455 (Gaiseric page), so they are taken out. The page gives no area.

region.text: coastal Numidia and parts of Mauretania

ledger.note: 435: peace with Rome makes the Vandal kingdom in Africa. 'Peace was made between the Romans and the Vandals in 435 through a treaty'; it left the Vandals coastal Numidia and parts of Mauretania as foederati (Gaiseric page: 'Vandal retention of Mauretania and part of Numidia as foederati'). The capital is Hippo Regius (infobox 435-439); the page does not say 'founded 435'.
439: the capital moves from Hippo Regius to Carthage (infobox: 'Carthage (439-534)').

region.text: Carthage and the Zeugitana around it

ledger.note: 19 October 439: Gaiseric takes Carthage. 'In a surprise move on 19 October 439, Gaiseric captured Carthage.'

region.text: Byzacena, Tripolitania and part of Numidia, with Proconsular Africa (the part inside the 443 shape)

ledger.note: 442: the treaty with Valentinian III. 'The Western Empire, under Valentinian III, secured peace with the Vandals in 442'; 'the Vandals gained Byzacena, Tripolitania, and part of Numidia' and confirmed 'Proconsular Africa'.

region.text: the Balearic Islands, Sardinia, Corsica and Malta

ledger.note: 455: the Vandals seize the islands. 'In 455, Gaiseric seized the Balearic Islands, Sardinia, Corsica, and Malta.'

June 455: the Vandals take Rome. 'The invasion culminated in his most famous exploit, the capture and plundering of Rome in June 455 AD' (landed 31 May; Pope Leo received Gaiseric on 2 June). It was a sack, not an annexation.
June 455: the Vandals leave Rome with their plunder. The pages give June 455 only and do not date the departure; a bridging entry.
468: Sicily. 'He occupied Sicily in 468 for 8 years until the island was ceded in 476 to Odoacer.' The Roman fleet of both empires was destroyed at Cape Bon the same year.

minus.text: Lilybaeum, the toehold in western Sicily

ledger.note: 476: Sicily is ceded to Odoacer. 'He gave Sicily to Odoacer in 476, in exchange for an annual tribute' (the Odoacer page: 'F. M. Clover dates this cession to September or October 476').

477: the Moors take Mauretania. After Gaiseric's death on 25 January 477 the Moors 'established more or less full control over the former province of Mauretania'; the Vandal Kingdom page has the Vandals 'rapidly losing territory in modern-day western Algeria to the Kingdom of Altava'.

region.text: the Aures Mountains (the Kingdom of the Aures dossier uses Batna and Khenchela)

ledger.note: 484: the Aures are lost for good. The Kingdom of the Aures 'was fully independent by the time of Huneric's death in 484 AD and never came under Vandal rule again'; Huneric 'completely lost control over the Aures Mountains to king Masties' (Vandal Kingdom page).

region.text: Lilybaeum, the toehold in western Sicily

ledger.note: 491: Lilybaeum goes to Theodoric. A footnote: 'Lilybaeum, a toehold in western Sicily, was ceded to Theodoric in 491'; the Vandal Kingdom page: Gunthamund 'lost large parts of Sicily to Theodoric's Ostrogoths'. The Odoacer page has the Vandals invading Sicily in 490.

region.text: the land south of Thugga seized by the Frexenses in 510

ledger.note: 510: the Frexenses take land south of Thugga. 'In 510 the Frexenses Berber tribe under king Guenfan seized a portion of territory south of Thugga', the Kingdom of the Dorsale. The disc is my reading of 'south of Thugga'.

region.text: Oea (Tripoli) and Sabratha, captured by the Laguatan

ledger.note: c. 510: the Laguatan take Tripoli. 'Around the 510s, migrating Laguatan berbers under king Cabaon captured Oea (modern Tripoli) and Sabratha'; the page gives the decade, so 510 is the decade's start.

533: Sardinia and Tripolitania rise. In Sardinia 'the local governor, Godas, declared himself an independent ruler'; in Tripolitania 'the native population, led by a certain Pudentius, rebelled against Vandal rule', both before the Roman fleet sailed (c. 21 June 533). Sardinia is not counted as lost: the Vandalic War page has Tzazon 'successful in re-establishing Vandal authority and killing Godas' before he left Sardinia to join Gelimer at Bulla, so the island stays Vandal until the conquest after Tricamarum. [Reviewer eu-06-d: Sardinia removed from this loss.]

region.text: Carthage and the Zeugitana around it

ledger.note: September 533: Carthage falls. The Romans landed at Caputvada in early September, 'met the Roman army at the Battle of Ad Decimum, near Carthage, on 13 September', and Belisarius's army entered Carthage on 15 September; Hilderic was executed as the army approached (Vandal Kingdom page).

region.text: the rest of the Vandal land: Byzacena, Zeugitana, Tripolitania and the islands

ledger.note: December 533: Tricamarum. 'In mid-December marched out of Carthage in the direction of the fortified Vandal camp at Tricamarum'; afterwards Belisarius 'had secured most of the provinces of Byzacena, Zeugitana and Tripolitania' and sent forces to Sardinia and Corsica, the Balearics and Septem.

March 534: Gelimer surrenders. 'It was not until March that the Vandal king agreed to surrender after receiving guarantees for his safety' (besieged on Mount Pappua); 'The Vandal Kingdom ended in 534 AD' (Vandal Kingdom page). The Praetorian prefecture of Africa was set up in April 534.

wars.name: Vandal conquest of Roman Africa
wars.outcome: The Vandals cross in 429, besiege Hippo Regius from 430 (14 months), win the treaty of 435 and take Carthage on 19 October 439.
wars.note: [Reviewer eu-06-d] Kept from the treaty of 435 (this state's first year) to the seizure of Carthage on 19 October 439; the crossing of 429 and the siege of Hippo Regius belong to the years before this state's start (the 'vandals' people row, Cliopatria 337-438).

wars.name: Vandal raid on Sicily
wars.outcome: Gaiseric besieged Panormus (Palermo) 'in 440 AD but was repulsed'. No land changed hands.

wars.name: Sack of Rome (455)
wars.outcome: Gaiseric lands on 31 May 455 and sacks Rome in June; the Vandals take the Balearics, Sardinia, Corsica and Malta the same year.

wars.name: Majorian's expedition against the Vandals
wars.outcome: Gaiseric strikes the Roman fleet at Carthago Nova (Cartagena, 460) before it sails and defeats it. No land changed hands.
wars.note: Vandal Kingdom page: 'assembled his fleet in 460'; the 461 date is only in a page title.

wars.name: Battle of Cape Bon (468)
wars.outcome: 'The last concerted effort by the two halves of the Roman Empire' fails at Cape Bon; Gaiseric occupies Sicily in 468.

wars.name: Berber wars of the Vandal kingdom

zones.text: the Aures Mountains (the Kingdom of the Aures dossier uses Batna and Khenchela)
the land south of Thugga seized by the Frexenses in 510
Oea (Tripoli) and Sabratha, captured by the Laguatan

wars.outcome: The Moors take Mauretania after 477, the Aures break away by 484, the Frexenses take land south of Thugga in 510, the Laguatan Oea and Sabratha in the 510s; Thrasamund's 523 expedition is defeated.
wars.note: The Vandal Kingdom page names the Aures, Altava, Frexenses and Laguatan; the Mauro-Roman Kingdom page dates the Aures to 484.

wars.name: Vandalic War
wars.outcome: Belisarius lands in September 533, wins Ad Decimum (13 September), Tricamarum (mid-December) and receives Gelimer's surrender in March 534; Byzantine Africa is the result.

certainty.note: The treaty lines of 435 and 442 are by province, not by survey, and the frontier with the Moors (Mauretania, Aures, Hodna) and with the Laguatan was never fixed; the island borders are coasts.

notes: Cliopatria's 439 shape is read as the 435 treaty land (Mauretanian and Numidian coast plus the Balearics, 85,012 km2) and the dossier starts in 435 with the capital at Hippo Regius; Carthage (439) is added by correction, since the shape has no Zeugitana. Sicily is drawn in Cliopatria from 441 to 489; the pages give a failed siege of Palermo in 440, occupation 468-476 and the Lilybaeum toehold to 491, so the 441-467 Sicily is a Cliopatria error. The Balearics, Sardinia, Corsica and Malta are 455 on the Gaiseric page (Cliopatria 439, 458 and 469). The Rome patch of the 455 shape (19 cells) is a sack of about a fortnight (dates not given). The 477 loss of Mauretania and the 484 loss of the Aures are from the Mauro-Roman Kingdom page; the Aures lie inland of the coastal Cliopatria shape, so that loss changes no cell. The Frexenses (510) and Laguatan (510s) have no dossier and no Cliopatria row: counterparts_needing_dossiers. The Vandal Kingdom page gives no area, so no infobox comparison was possible. Months: Carthage 19 October 439 (Gaiseric page); Ad Decimum 13 September and Carthage 15 September 533 (Vandalic War page, whose summary does not quote the entry itself); Tricamarum 'mid-December' on the Vandalic War page, 15 December on the Vandal Kingdom page; surrender in March 534. The 534 end year has no Cliopatria shape (the row ends 533); the dissolve event at 534 empties the 533 shape.
